thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging @eng-oncall and @sre oncall — sudden 8x spike in /v1/embeddings from a set of small IP blocks, started 10:12 UTC. Auto-mitigation suggested: enable geo-slice + short TTL WAF challenge for suspected vectors. See summary: 10:12-10:28 saw sustained 6k rps to embeddings endpoint (normal 700rps).
eng-oncall: Ack, I'm up. Pulling logs and kvcache metrics. Any obvious customer-facing errors?
sre-eli: Seeing lots of 429/503s for downstream batch workers, Instances queued, memory pressure on embedding pool. KV cache hit ratio unchanged. Likely a fanout scraper hitting async batch endpoint.
tiffany-ops: Notified pager and starting containment. @ingrid-ml can you confirm model variants being hit?
ingrid-ml: It's hitting the small-embed model (embed-small-v2) with short seqs. No sudden model rollouts. Appears programmatic: identical payload sizes and interval pattern.
leo-support: No major customer tickets yet, but one customer reported slow uploads ~10:20 and a single 502.
eng-oncall: Plan: (1) apply geo-slice throttling for suspicious ASN ranges (2) disable async batching for embeddings temporarily, route to direct low-concurrency path (3) add WAF challenge CAPTCHA on requests with high similarity fingerprint. Anyone object?
ingrid-ml: OK on model side. Disabling batching will increase cost but reduces fanout amplification.
tiffany-ops: I'll patch rate-limiter rules. Pushing incremental so we can rollback quickly.
eng-oncall: Executing quick commands now. Patch 1: add rate-slice policy for embedding route for X-IP-ranges, throttle to 60rps per-IP and global cap. Patch 2: disable batch-worker queue consumption for 20m.
eng-oncall: Command snippets:
```bash
# add rate-slice
redwoodctl policy add --route /v1/embeddings --matcher "ip_in_ranges:10.8.0.0/16,100.64.0.0/10" --rate 60/s --global-cap 2000/s --reason "scraper wave 2026-03-17"
# pause batch worker
redwoodctl workers pause --queue embeddings-batch --duration 20m --reason "mitigation: reduce fanout"
```
tiffany-ops: WAF rule staged: challenge mode for UA and fingerprint hashes that match >90% repeated payload hash pattern. Live in 2m.
eng-oncall: Rolling both changes.
incident-bot: Change deployed by eng-oncall at 10:22 UTC.
leo-support: Early signal — aggregate RPS dropped to ~1.2k within 3 minutes, error rate for customers returned to baseline for most. One high-volume customer still reports slower completion times ~10:30.
marketing: Heads up — could be visible to customers, are we drafting a notice?
customer-success: Let's prepare a short status banner for affected customers and include mitigation summary + ETA to fully restore. Low confidence on affected customer list until we correlate API keys.
ingrid-ml: Noted: the payload fingerprint suggests a scraper that retries with different IPs. Recommend adding token churn detection and raising quota for verified customers if blocked.
sre-eli: Found two ASNs spiking. Proposing to apply geo-fence on those ASNs and a short 5m heavier throttle then gradual ramp. Also enabling stricter connection timeouts at the edge.
eng-oncall: Applied ASN-level throttle + edge timeout changes. Edge config: keepalive 15s -> 5s for suspicious route.
incident-bot: ASN throttle applied at 10:26 UTC.
leo-support: Customer impact: Customer A (org_452) saw 30% increase in latency for embeddings between 10:18-10:28, then back to normal. Flagged for CS follow-up.
tiffany-ops: Monitoring dashboard: CPU/queue depth normalizing, error rates trending down. I'll keep batch disabled until next handoff unless we see regressions.
eng-oncall: PV: we'll do canary re-enable of batching at 10:50 if stable. Create rollback playbook in case of re-amplification.
ingrid-ml: Also recommend we add an automated eval to detect repeated identical payloads and auto-escalate to WAF challenge next time.
eng-oncall: Drafting short runbook entry now and will update the mitigation runbook with exact commands and thresholds.
marketing: We'll hold off on public comms until CS prepares a list and we confirm persistent customer impact.
customer-success: Preparing outreach for org_452 and any orgs with >20% latency regressions.
eng-oncall: Handoff to night oncall (sre-night) at 11:00 UTC. Summary: scraper wave targeted embeddings, we applied ASN & geo throttles, paused embedding batch queue, enabled WAF challenge, reduced keepalive, observed quick RPS drop and most customers back to baseline. Remaining action items: correlate API keys for blocked requests, add payload-fingerprint detector, create customer banner draft.
sre-night: Ack, I'll take post-11:00 monitoring and rollback if necessary.
incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Pager cleared at 11:02 UTC.
leo-support: Closing loop: created ticket CS-998 for customer follow-up and ENG-421 for runbook changes. :white_check_mark:
